prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1037; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Claimant reports neck and back strain and has indicated representation by counsel. All further contact to be routed through claimant's attorney.

Entry 2: Received notice of representation from claimant's attorney's office. Letter of representation on file. Requested itemized medical records and treatment history through counsel. Advised that a recorded statement from the claimant will be coordinated through the attorney.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos of both vehicles submitted by the insured. Rear bumper and trunk damage visible on the claimant's vehicle, consistent with reported impact. Damage estimate requested from the appraiser. Liability appears clear based on the initial police report, with the third-party driver cited for following too closely.

Entry 4: Spoke with claimant's attorney regarding the status of medical documentation. Counsel advised that the claimant is still undergoing physical therapy for neck and lower back strain and that treatment notes will follow once the provider releases them. Reminded counsel of the request for prior treatment history covering the past several years.

Entry 5: Received updated medical summary through counsel documenting ongoing treatment for cervical and lumbar strain, with a physician's note recommending continued therapy and reassessment. File flagged for supervisor review of bodily injury evaluation. No settlement offer extended at this time. Will follow up with counsel once the treating provider's final report is received.
